assessment: The paper provides evidence that a peptide from the nuclear pore protein Nup358 (RanBP2) forms a helix upon binding the dynein/dynactin adaptor BICD2 and is able to activate BICD2 in the same way as the small G-protein Rab6. Helix formation to activate BicD2 is a novel concept and will open up the search space for other potential activators that may be unstructured in their apo states.
